Can a single man who kills over four billion of his own kind be called righteous? No! He merely uses the guise of nature and justice to fulfill his own dictatorial desires.

And the Teutons claim they will drop all their nuclear bombs on Earth. Must we continue to stand by and watch him promote his 'justice'? Of course not! Because I believe that there are still good people, countrymen who refuse to yield to the Teutons, who want to continue the fight against the enemy!

......
strings.OMS_but_the_great_trial_still_ongoing: But the Great Trial is Still Ongoing!
strings.OMS_but_the_great_trial_still_ongoing_de:
......

Hear me! The Teutons' words are nothing but bluster. I have been fortunate enough to survive the nuclear strikes, and I have seen the true state of the so-called “£GFX_OMS_teutons_texticon Greater Germanic Reich”. The people of the Teutonic State are exhausted, and its national strength has dwindled. Adolf Hitler and your colleagues! If you can drop another nuclear bomb on Earth, then try! Your forces were already exhausted in the first Great Trial. Do you understand how long it takes to train a single effective soldier? The Teutons understand this point, of course.

Therefore, the rebels and the Teutons are merely blustering, attempting to use the deaths of billions to force the Black League into submission! But fortunately, we know the truth, and I will reiterate it: the Teutons have no soldiers left! We are more resolute now than ever. The civilization of Russia, thousands, even tens of thousands of years old, will never submit to despotism and dictatorship! We must rise up as a unified Black League, defeat the Teutons, and win this victory!

Long live the Black League!
Long live the Great Trial!

Crusaders, Advance!
strings.OMS_war_started_desc:
Our warriors have embarked on the journey once more. In this time of national crisis, we shall wage a total war. This is both a struggle for survival and our Second Great Trial.

However, time is too short. For now, we can only expand our army and awaken the sleeping martial spirit of our people. The effectiveness of the Black League's decades of reform will be demonstrated here, and the enemy will face our hammer of justice.

Earth is not a paradise; it is a struggle for survival.
strings.OMS_stockpile_in_bunker_desc: For this total war, we urgently need more equipment and weapons to support the front lines. We have a very expansive front, but we do not have enough troops to maintain it. Although we possess sufficient manpower, our existing stockpile alone cannot cover the terrifying equipment deficit. Fortunately, we control the largest original bunker network, which stores weapons and firearms from the past decade, and even half a century. We shall requisition all these weapons for the military to replenish our stocks.
strings.OMS_enforce_control_desc: Just as in the last Great Turmoil, we have once again acquired vast territories after decades of dormancy. Consequently, we face the same problem as before: insufficient control. The state apparatus is defunct in some areas, which is intolerable for a total war—think how much our war potential would increase if all these people were properly organized! For the total war, we shall rapidly strengthen local control to ensure the League operates efficiently.
strings.OMS_every_possible_people_desc:
And so, we can take the next step. After strengthening local control, the census of reservists has reached an unprecedented peak. Every person—yes, every single person—will be utilized with maximum efficiency within the League.

£GFX_OMS_dmitry_yazov_texticon Commander-in-Chief Yazov has ordered the search for available manpower within our controlled areas, and our loyal League soldiers shall swiftly execute this command.
strings.OMS_new_army: The Strong Army of the League
strings.OMS_new_army_desc:
Rejoice! The army of the Black League has been reborn from the ashes! The Black League's forces shall once again sweep away all enemies like a God of War, all thanks to the leadership of £GFX_OMS_dmitry_yazov_texticon Commander-in-Chief Yazov.

Our army has grown through combat, cast aside the vices of the past few years, and become a true, loyal force. We shall faithfully execute all commands from £GFX_OMS_dmitry_yazov_texticon Commander-in-Chief Yazov, and never again harbor rebellious thoughts.
strings.OMS_farmers_go_army_desc:
It seems our manpower is still insufficient. Since the atomic fire burned the world to ashes, manpower has hung over us like the Sword of Damocles. Now, the sword has fallen. Our war potential is reaching its limit...

...unless we take the next step. Even in this desperate situation, there is still a large number of useless institutions and people performing superfluous tasks, with farmers being a prime example. How dare they!? An action is imminent; the battlefield needs them.
strings.OMS_cut_the_bones: Cut the Fat, Keep the Bone
strings.OMS_cut_the_bones_desc:
We have purged those damned parasites, but it is not enough. Recent inspections have revealed an even more terrifying reality: even the bureaucrats performing so-called 'essential work' have a large number who are idling. And all this during a time of crisis! A large number of their so-called 'essential tasks' are fundamentally unnecessary. Soon, they will be dismissed and transferred to the Redemption Brigades as a warning to others.

The League has no need for these useless bureaucrats.
strings.OMS_waking_the_tiger_desc:
Our actions appear to be effective. After disbanding a significant portion of useless institutions, both manpower and industrial capacity have seen a noticeable improvement. How many resources were embezzled by those self-serving bureaucrats?

But that is no longer important. As factory output gradually increases, weapons are streaming off the assembly lines. The enemy will be overwhelmed by our terrifying industrial capacity.
strings.OMS_enemys_doing_desc:
Those madmen are back again.

They're starting to oppress the Russian people again for their 'Great Trial.' We were once so foolish as to let those lunatics unify Russia and be deceived and used by them, ultimately leading to this outcome. However, we cannot let them win again.
A race of life and death has begun.
strings.OMS_KMC_intelilgests_desc:
Arkhangelsk, the former capital of the Revolutionary Front. Now, Yuri Orlov—a great scientist, and the last intellectuals of Russia—are holed up here. They live by Spartan-like survival discipline, attempting to preserve the last spark of civilization.

But as long as the Black League and its followers exist for a single day, their goal will remain unattainable. They will come to understand this truth.
strings.OMS_support_them_business_desc: Need lab equipment? Take it! Need Rubles? I'll give you as much as you want! The knowledge they possess is priceless in the wasteland. As long as they cooperate with us, we'll give them whatever they ask for! Furthermore, we will send some personnel to help train their troops to ensure we can ultimately defeat the Black League.
strings.OMS_push_their_border_line_desc:
The Front's administrative personnel are limited. Frankly, we don't have the capacity to control most of West Russia and Moscow's territory, but we certainly can't surrender it and let the people ravaged by the wasteland suffer the Black League's aggression again.
We can only hand over these territories to this group of intellectuals. We wish them luck.
strings.OMS_the_old_enemy_desc:
Finland, ha, goddamn Finland. These animals once attacked the League at its most critical moment, leading to a catastrophic defeat. A decade or two ago, they also collaborated with the Nazis to occupy Karelia. They are undoubtedly goddamn Nazi collaborators, a bunch of animals worse than pigs and dogs.

But we truly have no choice. Omsk will undoubtedly attack Finland, and we must gather all our allies for the final struggle. Therefore, we must cooperate with these Finnish beasts, regardless of whether the people below like it or not. This is the final decision.
strings.OMS_but_we_can_only_coop_desc:
Alright, alright, alright. I know the rank-and-file soldiers all want to goddamn eat me alive for this news. But we have indeed established a cooperative relationship with Finland, and they are willing to contribute some personnel to resist Omsk.

During this much-needed breathing space, we can finally seize the vast territory of West Russia and bring its people under our protection. Those Finns are indeed animals, but at least they retain some semblance of humanity.
strings.OMS_oversea_loyalists_desc: After reaching an agreement with Finland, we have managed to contact forces in the former Baltic littoral and Belarus. There may be people there willing to cooperate with us. If so, we will assist them in opening a second front in the war against the Black League.
strings.OMS_anti_omsk_pact_desc:
There are still survivors along the Baltic coast. They are a faction comprised of Swedes, Finns, Norwegians, Latvians, and others. The current situation is remarkably similar to the Spanish Civil War half a century ago. Back then, too, a group of people from various countries sacrificed their lives for the same ideals.

We shall show the utmost respect to such a pure group of people. We will offer our greatest sincerity to bring them into our fold. They will not refuse, for they know well the consequences of refusal.
strings.OMS_old_wrrf_army_desc:
Outside Moscow, we still have our people in the former regions of Belarus and Ukraine. The renowned General Akhromeyev is fighting the remnants of the Black League there. We must try to bring him over; he would be glad to rejoin the Revolutionary Front.

More importantly, he has an armored division under his command.
strings.OMS_union_forever_desc: The situation on the Western Front is settled. The Red Army has been reborn, and we finally have the strength to fight the Black League. We shall remember the spirit of the Soviet Union, cherish the hopes of the people of the old era, and as the new chapter begins, eliminate the monstrous Omsk bandits from the Earth.
strings.OMS_meeting_with_YGR_desc:
The former Vorkuta region is now controlled by a group of anarchists. Like many anarchist experimenters, they practice mutual aid on the desolate Russian land.

However, this situation cannot last forever. One day—if not us, then those animals from the Black League—will shatter this peace. We must quickly unite them to lay the groundwork for our future operations on the Eastern Front.
strings.OMS_coop_like_1917_desc: During the Russian Civil War, the Black Army of Ukraine formed a united front to defeat the Whites. The current situation is far more severe than back then; a war that will determine the future of humanity is imminent. We must recreate the scene of 1917 and once again form a Pan-Left United Front.
strings.OMS_coop_like_1942_desc: During the Great Patriotic War, numerous anarchist partisans operated in the German-occupied territories. They delayed German forces and made significant contributions to our resistance. The current situation is far more severe than back then; a war that will determine the future of humanity is imminent. We shall recreate the scene of 1942 by supporting them with vast supplies, meeting the need for rear-area operations in the war against the Black League.
strings.OMS_YGR_frontier_to_OMS: Compress the Black League's Living Space
strings.OMS_YGR_frontier_to_OMS_desc: After making contact with sufficient forces, our operation begins. On the current land, all activities must rely on bunkers and survival clusters. We shall advance southward from the north, seizing the territories the Black League has failed to secure. Excluding areas where bunkers have been built, all uncontrolled regions will be ours.
strings.OMS_TOM_artist_city_desc: Although the Black League has repeatedly crushed the lands of Central Siberia, the spark of the Republic of Enlightenment has not been extinguished. The flame of reason and science still burns in Tomsk, and the philosophers still control the city. Even if the current situation can no longer support the existence of Salons, they still hope to establish a nation of liberty, equality, and fraternity. We shall swiftly extend an olive branch to prevent this light of reason from being extinguished.
strings.OMS_march_to_north_siberia_desc: There are still a few survivors on the vast plains of North Siberia, struggling to survive on that expansive wasteland. We cannot stand by and watch them suffer on the nuclear wasteland; we shall extend a helping hand and rescue them.
strings.OMS_arm_against_desc: Crusaders, are you ready!? A grand expedition is about to begin, and the fate of humanity depends on it. We shall train a corps of modern crusaders for the scholars of Tomsk. They will use tanks instead of armor, engines instead of horses, and fuel instead of blood. The Crusaders of Tomsk shall charge west and launch a fatal blow against the Black League.
strings.OMS_far_eastern_army_desc: By the shores of Lake Baikal, the chemical defense forces of the former Black League are based. They are true heroes, actively helping the populace on the current wasteland. They serve neither an ideology nor the 'Great Trial,' but the future of the Russian people. If we can talk to them properly, perhaps we can bring them into the Front?
strings.OMS_a_einheitfront_desc: They have agreed! After careful consideration, General Pikalov will join our cause and resist the Black League. The final piece on the Eastern Front has been played. Once all is settled, the war will begin immediately. It will be the first war of the new era and the last war of the old one.
strings.OMS_hard_union_desc: Just in case, we must resort to some... less honorable means. The Black League once developed LPC-70, which is a... very cruel chemical weapon, but we must use it. Since the Irkutsk chemical defense forces gave this to us, we must make good use of it. With a great enemy before us, life and death hang in the balance.
strings.OMS_Operation_Cerberus: Load the Operation Cerberus Focus Tree
strings.OMS_form_new_regiments_tt: A new unit will be deployed in our nation!
strings.OMS_priority_through_labor_tt:
We shall implement emergency measures.
The Maximum Work Hours and Forced Labor policy implementation rate will be set to 100%!
strings.OMS_soldiers_eat_first_tt:
We shall implement emergency measures.
The Military Training and Conscription System policy implementation rate will be set to 100%!
strings.OMS_last_light_tt:
This world is merely a barrel organ, and only God can play it.
All of us can only dance to the notes drawn from the bellows.
strings.OMS_decapitate_cerberus_tt: Unlocks the final solution against the £GFX_OMS_teutons_texticon Teutons.
strings.OMS_PT_2WRW_grand_offensive_stratagem_de: We shall transfer additional resources from the warehouses and launch a massive general offensive in the spirit of Comrade Yazov himself.
strings.OMS_PT_2WRW_ceaseless_assault_stratagem_: Our commissars will instill in our soldiers the patriotic fervor needed to relentlessly charge the enemy, never stopping until all reactionaries are eliminated.
strings.OMS_PT_2WRW_chemical_saturation_stratage: Extra planes, artillery, and rockets will be manufactured to carry more chemical weapons. A cloud of chemical warfare will sweep over the Germans as our soldiers march behind it.
strings.OMS_PT_2WRW_firestorm_assault_stratagem_: The plague of Germania will be eradicated by a firestorm that will burn down his fortresses, his homes, and his dreams. Just as scorched earth greeted the enemy when they marched on our Motherland, so too shall scorched earth greet the Teutons as our soldiers raze their nests.
strings.OMS_PT_2WRW_kill_em_all_desc: Where we tread, nothing shall live. This is what those Teutons deserve.
strings.OMS_no_control_trigger_tt: You have no power to control Yazov's actions.
strings.OMS_walk_through_the_forest_desc:
The Teutonic bandit gangs have been defeated.

Yazov stands on the platform temporarily erected at the bunker, with Ustinov and a host of generals behind him. His coat is heavy with glittering medals. Outside the bunker, an endless winter is dropping unceasing gray snow, dyeing the ruins—which can no longer be called a city—into a mass of gray, brown, and black. A fierce wind whistles, a sharp sound that offers a rushed, helpless little tune. The sun seems to have been extinguished, with only a few faint rays of light piercing the thick clouds, lighting a few candles for Omsk. In the 'square,' his only remaining soldiers stand in crooked, uneven formations. Beneath their tattered greatcoats are emaciated bodies, clutching rusty rifles. The cheers have long faded, and the euphoria of victory has cooled, leaving only this boundless silence and a soul that is increasingly hollow within the Marshal's uniform.

Looking at the silence before you, the twisted, fragile army, the fragmented, shattered homeland,

Yazov, were you truly right?
strings.OMS_POSTNUKE.37.t: How Many Miles to the Battlefield?
strings.OMS_POSTNUKE.37.desc:
It was a day a few years ago. Ar was attending school in Moscow. He had just turned 11, still the age for reading. He had a group of friends and a happy family. His mother was a full-time housewife, and his father worked at the nearby railway bureau.

One day, he was talking with his friend Terkot as usual. Terkot suddenly showed him something—an epaulet from the 'Russian National Revival Government' recently acquired from across the border. Ar was fascinated. After repeated requests, Terkot finally let Ar touch the epaulet from the east. At that moment, Ar was filled with an endless longing for war.

Soon, the 'Great Trial' began. Although the war had been going on for a long time, Ar still had no real concept of it; he was only interested in the cool uniforms and weapons. Then one day, an uninvited guest suddenly arrived in Moscow—the city was instantly thrown into a panic. Gunshots echoed everywhere, and citizens fled. A helicopter suddenly flew over Ar; others were too terrified to move, but Ar was ecstatic—his camera was recording! He captured the shocking sight of the helicopter flying overhead! Moreover, the pilot of the helicopter seemed to have looked at him. He rushed out of the school gate impatiently to chase the helicopter. Soon, the helicopter crashed in the city center park. Ar eagerly rushed over, wanting to admire the aircraft's beauty. To his delight, the person inside was alive! And he was holding a gun, a real gun! That was what he had always dreamed of. The person jumped out of the plane, and Ar excitedly asked him, \“Did you fly this plane? Did you crash?\”
The pilot merely pointed the gun at him, said nothing, and quickly leapt out of the aircraft.

Ar looked at the pilot; he was very young, completely lacking the air of a veteran, and utterly unlike the cold-blooded soldiers he saw on TV.

\“Can I touch your gun?\” Ar asked, moving closer to the pilot. Seeing this, the pilot quickly replied, \“I won't give you the gun, no matter how long you wait.\”
After a while, the pilot noticed the camera on Ar and suddenly offered to let him play with the gun. Ar rushed over without hesitation. However, he not only failed to touch the gun, but the pilot also took his camera. Just as the two were wrestling over the camera, Ar suddenly saw the epaulet on the man's shoulder—it was a Black League epaulet, identical to the one he had touched earlier. He stared intently at the epaulet. And so, they made a deal: Ar gave him the camera, and the pilot gave Ar his epaulet. As he was leaving, Ar asked the pilot's name, and this is what he replied:
strings.OMS_POSTNUKE.37.a: \“My name is Barnard, Barnard Viezmann. You can call me Barney.\”
strings.OMS_brutus_strikes_desc:
Like Brutus and Caesar, Yazov and his Black League have reached their end. Commander-in-Chief Yazov is now missing, and the Black League is in total chaos. Just as the Black League's followers hoped for someone to reclaim the League's leadership and maintain order, fate played a cruel joke on them. Dmitry Ustinov, a former West Russian Revolutionary Front general and the most trusted man by Commander-in-Chief Yazov after the Midnight, has personally destroyed the Black League's last possibility of resistance, ushering it into the final chapter of the old world.

Et tu, Brute? (And you, Brutus?)
strings.OMS_equalized_rationing_desc: Currently, the Black League and its cause are at their most precarious moment. A powerful Central Committee has been formed, which will allocate rations to individuals with maximum efficiency. Some might say this will sacrifice Russia's future, but what does it matter? We do not need a future with Teutonic remnants. No matter the cost.
strings.OMS_karbysevs_folly_desc:
Karbyshev, the founder of the theory, my mentor. I have never doubted the theory of the Great Trial. I have never betrayed the Great Trial. I have never... betrayed you. Where are you? I have searched for you in the woods for days, but you never appeared. Did you go to Utopia?

No, only now do I understand the profound meaning of your words. You realized that we were wrong. The 'Great Trial' was a farce from the very beginning. So you retreated into the dust, washed away your sins, and watch us from Utopia. And I have struggled in the mortal world, sought light in the eternal night, sunk into the mire of the swamp, unable to move, and finally recognized the truth after committing unforgivable sins in this world.

Now, Comrade Karbyshev, may I join you in Utopia? Or must I remain in hell forever?
strings.OMS_our_new_rome_desc:
The spirit of Rome has been reborn in Omsk. Commander-in-Chief Yazov is the Caesar of the Black League. We shall use our flesh and blood to help the Commander-in-Chief fulfill Karbyshev's will, paving the path of the Great Trial with blood.

We neither give nor ask for mercy. With sword in hand, there is no need for excuses for terror.
strings.OMS_ragnarok_desc:
Both sides are here. Countless years of hatred will be resolved here, and all things shall meet their end. The prelude to the old world's demise has ended, and the finale of the doomsday is now playing. On the desolate Earth—this lifeless planet—the survival of all civilization depends on this. The end of 'Fimbulwinter' was once thought to be the end of Ragnarök, but it was not the end of the beginning; it was only the beginning of the end. Malice and warfare engulf this planet, and everyone is fighting each other—everyone. When Hati and Sköll swallow the Sun and Moon, Ragnarök has arrived. Human civilization has been fortunate to survive until now, but can they survive until Ragnarök ends?

But when humanity truly experiences it,
Only when the plains turn into a sea of blood,
Only when the skies are filled with dark red light,
Only when there are no figures left standing on the battlefield,
Only when pillars of fire pierce the universe, igniting the earth and burning everything,
Will humanity know that 'Ragnarök' brings only endless pain and scars.
strings.OMS_the_hydra_slain_desc: We have finally decapitated the Hydra within the League. This brother of Cerberus and the Nemean Lion, which has caused countless harm, was full of evil, and was a tumor on the Black League, has finally been completely eradicated. It has now been entirely purged from our administrative organs, and the Hydra has been turned into a harmless, one-headed 'serpent.' We can finally refocus on the Great Trial.
strings.OMS_the_last_trial_desc:
The £GFX_OMS_great_trial_texticon Ragnarök£OMS_teutons_texticon has reached its climax. The doomsday finale plays a chilling score, with every note articulating humanity's sin and punishment. It speaks of the sin that has existed since the very beginning of creation, when humanity's first ancestors, Adam and Eve, chose the Forbidden Fruit for knowledge in the Garden of Eden. Yet, humanity ultimately cast aside emotion. The knowledge of 'discerning good and evil' is something only God has the right to possess, but man presumptuously claimed it, and thus sinned.

Then God unleashed His punishment: Ragnarök, which should have ended, continued to expand due to human greed. For a humanity consumed by avarice,
Even if the plains turn into a sea of blood,
Even if the skies are filled with dark red light,
Even if there are no figures left standing on the battlefield,
Even if pillars of fire pierce the universe, igniting the earth and burning everything,
Humanity will still charge to their death.

For those on the battlefield, their 'sin' is already unsurpassed; simply being alive is their greatest 'sin' and 'punishment.' To escape human retribution, they can only mechanically seek death on the battlefield to be freed from 'punishment.' And when they are freed, humanity's sin will grow greater. The sin of apathy toward life accumulates until finally, they no longer care how the world is, how the battlefield is, or how they themselves are. When they cast aside emotion, God's punishment has descended. Fire pierces the universe, smoke engulfs the mountaintops, and Yggdrasil, the World Tree that supports the cosmos, is consumed by flames and collapses. The unsupported world plunges into the surging sea, and the entire universe accelerates down the path called 'Destruction.' The doomsday finale is about to reach its end, and the prelude to destruction is about to begin. If humanity does not act now,
The stars will fall from the firmament, time will cease to exist, the scorched earth will tremble and sink into the tumultuous seabed, and the only thing visible will be towering waves. All that will remain in the universe is a great, eternal silence and everlasting darkness.
strings.OMS_the_omsk_redoubt_desc:
The prelude to doomsday has begun. Humanity faces 'Fimbulwinter.' The God of Light fell silent after a brief burst of immense light, and then fierce snow blew from all directions, enveloping the world in a deep winter. The skies soon became pitch black due to poisonous gas. The surface is covered everywhere by radioactive dust; God has brought down divine retribution on humanity. Without the sun, the world has lost its warmth. Amidst the biting cold, the prelude to doomsday reaches its climax. The orphans of the old world are struggling desperately, trying to survive the bitter cold. Suspicion and conflict pervade the planet. Since the light first shone across the world, war and malice have dominated it. In the face of reality, so-called 'democratic traditions' are meaningless. People are no longer tolerant, understanding, or mutually helpful to one another. Brothers kill one another, fathers and sons become enemies, murdering each other in ugly competition. The entire world has become deeply unsettled, and sin spreads like a plague.

The roosters 'Gullinbursti' and 'Fjalar' warn continuously, crowing until their voices are hoarse. The poison dragon hollowed out the deep roots of the World Tree to accommodate its offspring. Midgard's valleys and mountains vanished in the light, replaced by endless pits, visible even thousands of miles away. Soon after, the prelude to doomsday will end.

Humanity sighs at the close of the doomsday prelude, unaware that an even more brutal war awaits them. The horn of destruction is about to sound, and 'Ragnarök' is coming.
At that time, the chilling doomsday finale will begin...
strings.OMS_the_russian_spirit_desc:
\“I believe that Russia, above all else, will be unified, indivisible, and unconquerable.

I believe in my strength and the strength of my comrades.

I deny the lies of the Original Trial, and I recognize that the Black League will be the one and only salvation for Russia when the Day of Trial arrives.

Until that day, when the Great Trial comes, I shall share weal and woe with my comrades, I shall fearlessly face the enemy, and I shall dedicate my life to my Motherland.

I shall become Russia's sword and shield, extending justice for the fallen.

I swear this oath with my life to the sacred Russian Motherland.\”
strings.OMS_warriors_without_purpose_desc: Our soldiers have been corrupted. Decades of stagnation have caused the soldiers to lose their purpose; they no longer feel awe for the 'Great Trial.' Such an army cannot serve the Great Trial.
strings.OMS_yazov_GG.30.t: A Walk in the Woods, Part II
strings.OMS_yazov_GG.30.desc:
It is over. Snowflakes spin in the leaden-gray sky. The crunch of broken hinges as Yazov shoved open the wooden door startled a few sparrows from the eaves. The gas mask's filter canister was long overdue for replacement, and pale yellow droplets of liquid had condensed on the rubber facepiece's inner surface. He ripped it off too hard, leaving his cheekbones numb, and his first exhale of air carried a faint hint of almond. The moment his military hat slammed onto the table, the enameled black star chipped away a charred piece of wood from the corner. His gunpowder-soiled fingers immediately stiffened, only to gently trace the corner where a copper Russian coat of arms lay. Patina wrapped around the double-headed eagle like a spider's web; the left wing was broken in two, and the remaining gilt in the gloom cast a morbid light, like a dying eye.

Ustinov's hands, clutching his briefcase, were trembling. The gold foil of the party emblem on the leather cover had long been worn away, revealing brown cracks underneath, like an old scar. He stood three paces from the fireplace, afraid to move further. The mud on his boot soles, mixed with tiny pieces of ice, had begun to melt.

The portrait of Karbyshev above the fireplace was burning. Not from direct flame-lick, but the canvas edge had curled to a charred black, slowly shrinking inwards, revealing the mottled bullet marks on the wall behind. The subject's eyes were darkened by smoke; the once keen gaze had become murky, and the line on his mouth that symbolized resolve now looked like a deep furrow pressed by suffering.

Yazov just stood there, the back hem of his greatcoat still dripping water, forming small puddles on the floor. He stared at the flames on the portrait, the light flickering in his pupils, bright and dim, as if conducting a silent judgment.

\“Comrade Commander-in-Chief,\” Ustinov's voice had the rustle of rubbing paper. He pulled a few documents from his briefcase. \“The Moscow celebration report, and also...\”

\“Read.\” Yazov's voice sounded like two rusty iron plates grating together.
\“Yes.\” Ustinov cleared his throat and purposely raised his voice. \“During the Red Square parade, the masses spontaneously organized a chorus of ten thousand people; Barnaul has overfulfilled its grain delivery quota, and the kolkhoz representative said on the radio...\” He stopped abruptly.

The moment Yazov turned around, Ustinov saw the ice particles clinging to his eyelashes. The next second, his collar was gripped tightly, and the second button of his suit flew off, clanging against the fireplace's iron plate. The documents scattered across the floor. On one photo, the joyous, cheering faces of children holding flowers were rapidly blurred by the muddy water on the floor.

He slammed Ustinov onto the ground. Documents were strewn everywhere. On one conscription report, next to the officer's signature, was a small line written in pencil: 'One crate of canned goods for every five quotas.' Yazov stared at the line, then suddenly covered his face and squatted down, a suppressed sob escaping his throat, like a wounded bear licking its wounds in the depths of its cave.

Ustinov lay on the ground, not daring to move. He saw tears seeping through Yazov's fingers, hitting the dusty floor, leaving small, dark spots. Those tears quickly froze, like transparent grains of salt.
After what felt like an eternity, the fire in the fireplace gradually subsided, leaving only a few glowing red embers. Yazov stood up, the tear tracks on his face frozen into white streaks of ice, his eyes utterly vacant.

\“I'm going out,\” he said.
\“Comrade Commander-in-Chief, the situation outside is...\”
\“I'm going to the forest.\” Yazov cut him off, picking up the button that had flown off and putting it in his coat pocket. \“I'm going to see Karbyshev.\”

When Ustinov left, only Yazov and the slowly burning portrait remained in the room. Karbyshev's face was burned into a blurry silhouette, like a shadow gradually receding into the distance.

On the snow in the forest, shell casings that had not been cleaned up still lay. Yazov walked across the deep snow, each step growing heavier. He once thought he was the helmsman of this ruined nation, but now he understood that he was merely a sail torn to shreds by the storm, without control over even his own drifting direction.

The wind whipped snow onto his face, like tiny needles. He pulled the rusty coat of arms from his pocket and placed it before the tombstone. Snow fell upon it, quickly accumulating a thin layer, like a white shroud covering this once-symbol-of-glory.

Scattered gunfire could be heard in the distance, likely the anti-government forces attacking the checkpoint again. Yazov did not turn back, standing quietly, watching the snowflakes dance before the tombstone, like countless white butterflies circling, then falling, finally merging with the earth.

\“Call me a car,\” Ustinov said,
strings.OMS_yazov_GG.30.a: \“I need to go to Omsk now, immediately.\”
strings.OMS_yazov_GG.29.desc:
The bunker's ventilation fan emitted an asthmatic wheeze, shattering the halo of the kerosene lamp. Water seeping from the concrete walls soaked the map, blurring the contours of the Ural Mountains into an unverified memory. Twenty pairs of military boots struck the floor in unison, the echo rebounding off the steel dome like some belated death knell.

Ustinov's fingers twisted the clasp of his briefcase, leaving red marks. The cracks in the leather surface were clogged with dust from years of accumulation, as if locking the secrets of those years into the creases. He cleared his throat, the bob of his Adam's apple cutting a rigid arc in the gloom: \“Comrades should be aware that the recent communication frequency... is not normal.\”

The Armored Commander sitting in the front row suddenly straightened his back, the reflection from his medals sweeping across the tense faces of those present. Someone instinctively reached for the sidearm on their hip; the slight metallic click of the safety latch echoed throughout the bunker, like a fuse about to be ignited.

\“I'll be blunt,\” Ustinov's fingernails dug into the edge of his briefcase. \“Commander-in-Chief Yazov has been out of contact for seventy-two hours. All we found in the snow of the forest park was this.\” He pulled half of a corroded coat of arms from his bag; the right wing of the double-headed eagle was completely severed, and dark brown ice shards were frozen onto the broken edge. As his fingertip passed over the rust, everyone fell silent.

The murmur of discussion crackled like damp gunpowder. The Chief of Operations' pen traced a disorganized zigzag line on his notepad, before the tip abruptly punctured the paper. The list of 'traitors' slated for execution tomorrow was written there.

\“The reason for calling all of you together...\” Ustinov's voice suddenly caught. His eyes scanned the familiar faces in the crowd; one man's cuff was still stained with blood from suppressing protests. He suddenly tugged at his tie, his throat bobbing violently. \“Is to discuss...\”

The lock on the briefcase snapped open without warning.

It wasn't the soft click of metal engaging, but the sharp ping of a spring breaking. The first things to fly out were several pages of burning documents; the flames glowed a strange blue in the oxygen-starved bunker, illuminating the terror that exploded in Ustinov's pupils. Then came a muffled roar, like a gagged explosion. The heat wave instantly overturned the conference table, tearing the map of Russia's borders into a flurry of paper butterflies.

Half of the Chief of Operations' arm was caught on the ventilation fan; his military tag spun between the blades, the engraved name blurred by centrifugal force into a smear of light. Someone tried to crawl towards the emergency exit but was pinned by a collapsing steel rebar; the screams were quickly choked off by thick smoke. Ustinov last saw the coat of arms falling from the air, briefly glowing in the flames like a dying star.

Three days later, when anti-government forces blasted open the bunker's iron door, snow was pouring in through the bullet holes. Seventeen bodies were frozen in distorted postures. One of them was still holding a pen, his stiff fingers clamping a half-finished victory report; the ink on the phrase 'Ten Thousand Jin Per Mu' had bled out, like a puddle of congealed blood.

When the trucks transported the bodies to Red Square, crows were pecking at the unburnt celebration streamers. Someone recognized Ustinov's frozen, purple face. It was this face that had promised them 'there will be bread' at their village entrance years ago. Now, fragments of his briefcase were mixed with countless artillery shells, glinting coldly in the snow.

After the spring thaw, a hunter found half a Black League medal in the forest. The name on it was blurred by rainwater, and the coat of arms was already covered in moss. Only on the side facing the sun could the residual lines of the double-headed eagle be seen faintly fluttering in the wind, as if narrating a story buried under the dust.
strings.OMS_yazov_GG.29.a: In nihilum nil posse reverti, ex nihilo nihil fit.
strings.OMS_soldiers_eat_first_desc:
\“He held seven stars in his right hand, and a sharp two-edged sword came from his mouth. His face was like the sun shining in its strength.\” —Revelation 1:16
Allocatable resources are stretched thin, but we must prepare for the Great Trial while also maintaining the most basic social order. What should we do? The answer is obvious: prioritize all resources for the military.

As true citizens of Russia, one must have the spirit to contribute all their resources, as the oath says, \“I shall dedicate my life to my Motherland.\” Now is the time of the final trial, and the oath must be protected.

Whether farmer, worker, entrepreneur, or soldier, all must act under the oath. The Black League's oath is an unchangeable iron law. Russia needs them now, it needs everyone,

Including you, sitting in front of your screen.
strings.OMS_the_last_supper_desc:
\“After this I saw another angel coming down from heaven, having great authority; and the earth was illuminated with his glory.
And he cried out with a mighty voice, saying, 'Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great! It has become a dwelling place of demons, a prison for every unclean spirit, and a cage for every unclean and hateful bird.
For all the nations have drunk of the wine of the passion of her immorality, and the kings of the earth have committed immorality with her, and the merchants of the earth have become rich by the abundance of her luxury.'\”
—Revelation 18:1, 18:2, 18:3

The Final Trial has arrived. Midgard's winter will turn into an inferno, flames rising. The flames of war have spread from Vanaheim to Asgard.
As the Teutons treated us, so shall we treat the Teutons; we shall repay the Teutons double for their deeds.

The doomsday finale will play.
strings.OMS_a_circle_of_judases_desc:
The ninth circle of Hell is the icy realm for traitors, the farthest from God.
Because her sins are piled up to heaven, God has remembered her iniquities.
'The woman was clothed in purple and scarlet, and adorned with gold and precious stones and pearls, having in her hand a gold cup full of abominations and of the unclean things of her immorality.'
—Revelation 18:6, 18:7

The light symbolizing the Hydra has come on again; an action that will shake the League is about to begin...

The day the doomsday finale plays is drawing closer.
strings.OMS_fields_of_rot_desc:
And the angel took the censer, and he filled it with the fire of the altar, and hurled it to the earth; and there were peals of thunder and sounds and flashes of lightning and an earthquake.
The first angel sounded, and there came hail and fire, mixed with blood, and they were hurled to the earth; and a third of the earth was burned up, and a third of the trees were burned up, and all the green grass was burned up.
The second angel sounded, and something like a great mountain, burning with fire, was hurled into the sea; and a third of the sea became blood.
And a third of the living creatures that were in the sea died, and a third of the ships were destroyed.
The third angel sounded, and a great star fell from heaven, burning like a torch, and it fell on a third of the rivers and on the springs of waters.
—Revelation 8:5, 8:6, 8:7, 8:9, 8:10

The day the doomsday finale plays is drawing closer.
strings.OMS_the_hearts_decay_desc:
\“Blessed is he who reads and those who hear the words of the prophecy, and heed the things which are written in it; for the time is near.\”
—Revelation 1:3

We are facing unprecedented challenges. Combat is increasingly grinding, survival pressure is growing daily, and the League's heart is slowing down.
If so, we need a powerful 'electric shock' to the heart, giving it immense impetus to pump new blood.

This will certainly overdraw the League's future, but what does the future matter? Our hatred for the invading enemy is eternal; we must burn everything, including our future. So long as justice prevails, even if the world is destroyed.

The day the doomsday finale plays is drawing closer.
strings.OMS_ghosts_of_karbyshev_desc:
\“and He will wipe away every tear from their eyes; and there will no longer be any death; there will no longer be any mourning, or crying, or pain; for the first things have passed away.\”
—Revelation 21:4

Comrade Karbyshev, were my actions right or wrong?

Now that the Final Trial is here, I have issued one extermination order after another against the Teutons, and the soldiers are carrying out my will. But why do I always feel, why do I feel increasingly distant from you? Every time I issue a command, I hope that you will be there, guiding me, educating me, but you are often absent. These days, I am sleepless every night, hoping that I can find you, that I can talk to you again.

Can you tell me if I was right or wrong, Commander-in-Chief Karbyshev?
strings.OMS_beneath_my_skin_desc:
\“I know your deeds and your toil and perseverance, and that you cannot tolerate evil men, and you put to the test those who call themselves apostles, and they are not, and you found them to be false.\”
—Revelation 2:2

What exactly is the definition of a life as a 'human'? We don't need to ponder this.

A citizen of the Black League must shoulder both civilian duties and the constant responsibility of a soldier. A soldier must obey the League's commands. When faced with a threat, a soldier must step forward, forging the Great Trial with blood.
Now that the Great Trial is about to restart, a soldier must serve the Great Trial, making themselves a gear in the great system, operating at all times beyond their limit, even if it endangers their life. This is the duty of a League citizen.
strings.OMS_finding_a_surplus_desc:
\“The fifth angel sounded, and I saw a star from heaven which had fallen to the earth; and the key of the bottomless pit was given to him.\”
—Revelation 9:1

A war that spans the globe requires all of humanity to serve it.

This Great Trial must utterly destroy the Teutons' life force. To this end, we must reclaim the legacy of the Great Trial. During the last Great Trial, we established a series of weapon caches across Russia to ensure we had sufficient arms to destroy the Teutons.

Now is the time of need. We shall search for the weapon caches from the Great Trial era. Although the records for many caches have been lost, and some armories may well have been looted, even if a single gun is discovered, it will be worth it.
strings.OMS_activate_the_spetsgruppa_desc:
\“The nations were enraged, and Your wrath came, and the time came for the dead to be judged, and the time to reward Your bond-servants the prophets and the saints and those who fear Your name, the small and the great, and to destroy those who destroy the earth.\”
—Revelation 11:18

The 'Vympel' Spetsgruppa has always been the Black League's internal backbone. In the Commander-in-Chief's eyes, with the front lines strained and reserves being consumed like a tide, the most elite reserve force within the League is now 'Vympel.' After careful consideration, we have decided to integrate the Vympel unit into the military command structure and dispatch it to the front lines for combat.

Their experience in urban counter-terrorism operations will be greatly beneficial in the fight to clear out the bunkers.
strings.OMS_loyalty_through_deed_desc:
\“And they overcame him because of the blood of the Lamb and because of the word of their testimony, and they did not love their life even when faced with death.\”
—Revelation 12:11

If we lack a strong will, then the most sophisticated weapons and equipment are mere talk.

In the Commander-in-Chief's view, a true military unit must have an unyielding will, express loyalty through action, and faithfully execute commands. Even if we pull all our security forces to the front line, what good is it? If they lack a strong will, they will only scatter like birds and break rank. We will teach our soldiers how to cultivate an unyielding will.
strings.OMS_exorcise_defeatism_desc:
\“and he said with a loud voice, 'Fear God, and give Him glory, because the hour of His judgment has come; worship Him who made the heaven and the earth and sea and springs of waters.'\”
—Revelation 14:7

Well, there are always people who continuously become defeatists, constantly saying things like we 'can't win,' just like during the Great Stagnation decades ago. What exactly are they trying to achieve? These defeatists are always incompetent and detrimental. They're good for nothing but blatant lies! I must make an example of them to stop this behavior.

The day the doomsday finale plays is drawing closer.
strings.OMS_infiltrate_the_cliques_desc:
\“So the first angel went and poured out his bowl on the earth; and it became a loathsome and malignant sore on the people who had the mark of the beast and who worshiped his image.\”
—Revelation 16:2

Even though we have returned to the surface, there are still some warlord-like organizations lurking in unseen corners. The damage they inflict on the Black League is immeasurable. In the past, we would likely have annihilated these organizations directly; but now, we will incorporate them into our order of battle and let them fight the Teutons.

If they are willing, this is naturally the best solution. If they are unwilling, then we will go and make them willing.
strings.OMS_investigate_the_army_desc:
\“And I saw heaven opened, and behold, a white horse, and He who sat on it is called Faithful and True, and in righteousness He judges and wages war.\”
—Revelation 19:11

What exactly are those people in the military doing? Frontline reports always declare our great victories, yet the resources we consume are increasing daily.

Before the nuclear war, the Bureau of Observation and Statistics was responsible for such matters, but it was dissolved during the Great Stagnation. Now, the Bureau of Observation and Statistics will be re-established, and its powers will be immensely expanded. Desperate times call for desperate measures, and an investigation targeting the military will be swiftly launched.
strings.OMS_interrogate_the_citizenry_desc:
From his mouth comes a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations. He will rule them with a rod of iron, and he treads the winepress of the fierce wrath of the Almighty.
“—Revelation 19:15

There are also traitors among the citizens within the gathering places, who have become lazy and have adopted the despicable habits of the Teutonic people.

To ensure the victory of the Great Judgment, the Commander-in-Chief will launch an investigation to uncover the saboteurs hiding within the League. Such parasites must not be allowed to continue their sabotage; their crimes will be made public.
strings.OMS_smashing_the_mask_desc:
A worthy and excellent citizen of the Black League must remember:
\“I firmly believe that Russia, above all else, shall be united, indivisible, and unconquerable.

I firmly believe in my strength, and the strength of my comrades.

I deny the lie of the initial 'Trial,' and I acknowledge that the Black League, when the Day of Trial arrives, shall be Russia's sole and only salvation.

Until that day, the Great Trial arrives, I shall share weal and woe with my comrades, I shall face the enemy without fear, and I shall give my life for my Motherland.

I shall become the sword and shield of Russia, to extend justice for the fallen.

I shall place my loyalty to the Black League above all other things.

I swear this oath upon my life to the Holy Russian Motherland.\”

The day the Finale plays is closer.
strings.OMS_priority_through_labor_desc:
They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more; neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat.
—Revelation 7:16

If a machine's gears lack lubrication, the efficiency of that machine's operation will rapidly decline. Clearly, due to insufficient rations, factory output is gradually decreasing. The workers need to be given more resources and more rations.

Some might consider this a \“socialist practice,\” but honestly, we give rations not because of our great compassion, but because it can effectively increase production efficiency.
strings.OMS_hunger_penalization_desc:
Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.

—Revelation 2:10

After all, our resources do not grow on trees. More resources in one place means fewer resources in another.

We need to prioritize rewarding citizens who perform excellently. This will cause many excellent citizens to be unable to serve the Great Trial; they will never see the day the Great Trial ends. But this is a necessary evil.

The day the Finale plays is closer.
strings.OMS_formalize_the_scouts_desc:
And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God. And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.
—Revelation 19:13-14

Manpower is insufficient, far from enough. As the new youth of the League, it is their responsibility to shoulder the burden in the most critical moment!

Now is the most critical moment for the entire League. We will incorporate adolescents, and even children, into the order of battle. Perhaps this is a crime against humanity, perhaps this will cause us to lose the future, but when the Great Trial ends, as long as one Russian is alive, that will be our victory.
strings.OMS_equalize_the_rationing_desc:
And I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Write, Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.
—Revelation 14:13

After a brief accident, we will further refine the rationing system currently in place.

We will precisely calculate the necessary rations for each type of work and distribute exactly enough supplies to meet their needs, so as to utilize available resources with the highest efficiency. For the army, we will spare no effort to ensure the highest level of supply; even if producing one extra unit of supplies allows us to kill one more Teuton, that is a great victory for us.
strings.OMS_decapitate_cerberus_desc:
And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever.
—Revelation 20:10

Solomon! Look at the serious crime you have committed!?

When we truly advance westward, we can clearly see that those former enemies have crawled out of the ground, attempting to continue their presence on our land to obstruct us. Their very existence is a blasphemy against the Great Trial. We must utterly eliminate these despicable servants.

Cerberus is dead.
strings.OMS_last_light_desc:
And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God.
—Revelation 21:3

What is a dream? A dream is the continuation of reality.
What is reality? It is the end of a dream.

We have already advanced into the Teuton lands. They are still dreaming that they can escape their past sins and be forgiven by the Lord again, but the bloody reality is right before their eyes. It's time to wake up from the dream.
strings.OMS_counting_time_desc:
The setting sun nails the shadows of the routed soldiers to the scorched earth, and unit designations shatter into paper ash in the wind. The rust of rifles seeps into palms like undried blood. This army has long become a sieve, the names on the roster chipped away one by one by death, leaving only despair murkier than the trench water in the eyes of the survivors.

The remnants of the military banner are wrapped around a broken rifle, flying like a shroud. Every wound cries out for debt, and every uncollected corpse awaits an explanation. The so-called reckoning is nothing more than forcing the routed soldiers to march forward over the bones of their own, until they repay the blood owed, drop by drop, to this land scorched by artillery fire.

Though the country is broken, the rivers and mountains remain, and in the city in spring, grass and trees grow deep.
strings.OMS_falling_ash_desc:
The Black League has fallen.

The lights of the old command post have long been extinguished; the orders that once commanded the steel torrent are now phosporescence in the scorched earth. With every gust of night wind, half a line of faded military orders drifts into the ranks of the Redemption Brigade. They tread in their ignorance, their boot heels crushing the scorched earth, the dust wrapped with fragments of yesterday's medals.

Finally, the obsession is incinerated along with the troop roster. Only in solitude does one realize with a start that both fear and that pure hatred have long been preserved as specimens in the ashes.

You witness a martyrdom destined to spiral out of control, and in the afterglow of nothingness, you claim a boundless freedom.

\“Dmitry Timofeyevich, did you ever feel that you were being watched?\”

Now, Yazov gives his answer...
strings.OMS_the_illusion_undone_desc:
Yazov, did you see it?

The fog is seeping in through the cracks of the bunker.

The \“Abundance\” and \“Peace\” in the report gleam so brightly, but even the most beautiful words cannot hide the bloody truth behind them—the stench of the starved, the smell of death. The Black League's medals are dazzling in the sunlight, but what polishes them is the fig leaf of lies.

Standing in the gap between data and truth, watch the grassroots reports grow wings, carrying falsehoods to the clouds; while on the ground, frozen hands still clutch half a piece of bark. The so-called illusion is merely someone painting a sugar coating of ink over suffering, so that everyone who swallows it tastes the sweetness of glass.

You may not have realized it yet, but Man is a wolf to his fellow man.
strings.OMS_darkness_in_the_west_desc:
The conscription roster yellows on the windowsill where the west wind blows, and the ink's \“fifteen\” is gnawed by time into \“eighty.\” The bones of those youths sent to the battlefield have long grown into the scorched earth of the Western Front; only urns of ashes roll back with the west wind, the names of their hometowns carved on the urn mouth blurred into scars by the ashes.
Wind from the west always carries the echo of gunfire. Look at the returnee squatting by the desolate grave, burying the urns of ashes one by one. With each burial, he plants a sprig of wild wormwood into the urn's mouth—the grass they used to weave wreaths in childhood, now standing crookedly at the grave, like a series of muster calls that never sounded.
The so-called journey home is merely the west wind blowing the shadows of youth into a handful of dust.

The Huai Mountains are faint, a thousand li of cloud-capped peaks holding a thousand li of sorrow. The Huai River flows long, ten thousand acres of misty waves holding ten thousand acres of grief.

Mountains are long and waters are distant, blocking the traveler's eastward gaze. Grieving the old and the new sorrow, tearful and speechless facing the late spring.
strings.OMS_light_from_the_east_desc:
The Black League's guard towers are plunged into the scorched earth of Eastern Europe like withered nails.

Artunin hides in a snow cellar in the forest, hammering a sickle with a melted artillery shell casing, sparks splashing onto the patches of his tattered greatcoat: it was a comrade's uniform, its stitching still embedded with shrapnel from last deep autumn.

He always carries a drawing wrapped in plastic cloth, a crooked sun given by a child from his hometown. The paint on the drawing is darkened by smoke, but its edges are polished bright from being touched. Villagers sneak into the snow cellar late at night; an old woman hands him a frozen, hard potato, a hunter offers a rifle with old carvings, and even deserters come to defect with Black League deployment maps.

Lux in tenebris lucet.
strings.OMS_postnuke_time_tt: All has ended, time is meaningless.
strings.OMS_postnuke_time_delayed_tt:
The sky is gradually stained crimson,
swallowed by an ebony-like darkness.

Innumerable stars, consumed entirely,
wither and pile up like phantoms.
Thoughts drift upward in the solitary night sky, splitting apart.

Every time this world changes its form,
even the things one wishes to protect,
will also be destroyed along with it.

My heart is restless, filled with the dark color of immorality.
I am pierced by the cold, feeling stripped bare.
Even if I continuously chase after a vague, illusory goal,
I will never reach the destination.
Then what exactly am I fighting for?
If the light slowly fades and loses its luster,
even if this water planet is destroyed,
I cannot forget this small wish,
which guides me to where I should be.

Ashen like white snow, falling from your sky.
Ashen like white snow, making me ponder why I must fight.
Thoughts drift upward in the solitary night sky until they break,
Dispelling the darkness and exchanging it for glory,
seems overly illusory and hollow.

I was wounded by scattered fragments and walked this far.
strings.OMS_cries_from_the_ash_desc: The earth is burning, and the sky is weeping. We won the war, but we lost everything. Cities have been reduced to rubble, fields turned into scorched earth, and survivors cling to life amidst the ruins; in their eyes, there is no longer the fanaticism for the \“Great Trial,\” only endless emptiness and despair. Marshal Yazov walks across this land of silence, every step falling upon the ashes of his former comrades. What he sees is not the glory of victory, but the gravestone of civilization. The sound carried on the wind is not a triumphal song, but the wailing of countless departed souls. Black flakes fall from the leaden sky, covering the twisted steel and broken concrete—that is not snow, but dust condensed with radiation and death. The air is thick with an unspeakable odor, a blend of rusting metal, decaying corpses, and acrid chemicals, the very breath of this dying world. The fanatic belief that once sustained the Black League now appears utterly pale and ridiculous before this absolute silence. The hatred that propelled the soldiers forward has, with the total disappearance of the enemy, become a blade that turns back on itself. Now, they must face an adversary more terrifying than any enemy: a future without hope, one they created with their own hands. And Yazov, the chief architect of it all, must be the first to complete this pilgrimage to hell.
strings.OMS_whispers_in_the_ranks_desc: The euphoria of victory is fading at a visible speed, replaced by endless drudgery and suffocating despair. The soldiers are no longer war machines chanting slogans; they are men, flesh and blood who feel fatigue, fear, and confusion. In the chilling wind of the nuclear winter, by the flickering campfires, and within the filthy bunkers, whispers begin to spread like a plague. They talk about their fallen comrades, whose vibrant faces are now just cold name tags; they talk about faraway family, wondering if they are still alive in this wasteland; they begin to talk about the meaning of this war, a topic once beyond question. The seed of doubt, once planted, grows wildly in the soil of despair, blossoming into the flower of betrayal. Political commissars find that their rousing speeches now elicit only the soldiers' numb and skeptical glances. The ideological dam that held this army together is slowly being eroded by the bitter tide surging from within, cracking open countless tiny yet fatal fissures. The once-impregnable Black League now rings with hollow echoes.
strings.OMS_oh_karbyshev_desc:
Comrade Karbyshev, founder of the theory, my eternal mentor. I have never had a single doubt about the theory of the \“Great Trial,\” I have never betrayed your grand vision, I... I have never betrayed you. Where are you? I have searched for you for days in this forest scorched by fire, yet you have never appeared. Did you, perhaps, also go to that so-called Eden you spoke of?

No, I only now understand the profound meaning of your words. You had already realized that everything we did was wrong, that the \“Great Trial\” was a complete farce from the very beginning. And so you retreated into the dust, cleansing yourself of all your sins, and watch us from that vague utopia. But I, I have been struggling in the sea of human suffering, trying to chase a flicker of light in the endless night, sinking into the quagmire, unable to move anymore. Only after committing unforgivable sins in this mortal world did I finally recognize the truth.

Now, Comrade Karbyshev, may I accompany you to Eden? Or am I destined to remain in this bottomless hell, until eternity?
strings.OMS_look_at_me_now_desc: The phantom of Karbyshev appears more and more frequently in Yazov's dreams and reality. He is no longer the benevolent, resolute mentor of his memory, but a silent judge, an embodiment of Yazov's conscience. His gaze seems to pierce the barriers of time and space, questioning Yazov: Is this the Russia you wanted? Is this the future you promised? Is this the result of what you have done in my name? Yazov tries to escape, burying himself in endless official duties, attempting to numb himself with alcohol and drugs, but he cannot shake off that omnipresent gaze. Whether in front of the operational map or in the depths of a midnight dream, those eyes are always there, quietly staring at him. He must face the world he created, face the lies and sins within his heart. He can no longer hide behind his mentor's shadow; he must step forward and look straight at the true self he has long been afraid to acknowledge. In this trial, there is no judge, no court, only him and his sins.
strings.OMS_ghosts_from_the_past_desc:
The war is over, but the ghosts of war have not departed. They lurk in the shadows of the ruins, roam the nightmares of the survivors, and, like maggots on bone, infest Yazov's mind. The people he killed, the people he failed, the countless comrades and enemies who died because of him—all have become relentless nightmares, permanent residents in his personal hell. He cannot sleep, he cannot find peace; the boundary between wakefulness and dream has become blurred. He is imprisoned by his past sins, agonizingly wandering the border between reality and hallucination. His guards and subordinates notice that the Marshal has become increasingly solitary and eccentric; he often talks to empty corners or lets out startled cries in the dead of night. The Supreme Commander of the Black League is being devoured by his own war; he himself is turning into a ghost of the old era.

Non omnis moriar...
strings.OMS_tears_in_the_rain_desc:
The sky pours down black rain, every drop carrying the dust of radiation, washing over this ravaged earth. The rain cannot cleanse the sin; it only exposes the wounds, making the pain more acute. In this ceaseless rain of mourning, Yazov's inner defense completely collapses. He no longer struggles, no longer rages, only boundless sorrow remains. He seems to see a different world that could have been. A world without war, without hatred, where children could run in the sun and old people could play chess peacefully in the parks. That world was once within reach, like a flower in the mirror or the moon in the water, beautiful and fragile. But that world, along with the possibility of its existence, has been destroyed by his own hands. This black rain is the tears of the entire planet, shed for the crimes he committed. At this grand funeral, Yazov is both the chief mourner and the sole sinner; he weeps for everything he buried, yet he cannot utter a sound.

Tempus edax rerum.
strings.OMS_yazov_GG.28.desc:
Sleep has become a torture more terrifying than death for Yazov. Every time he closes his eyes, attempting to find a moment of peace, countless faces swarm out of the darkness, dragging him into the abyss of memory. There are the political commissars he ordered executed for \“ideological unreliability,\” their eyes filled with incomprehension and disappointment before death; there are the young soldiers torn apart by artillery fire on the battlefield, still shouting \“Urah!\”; there are the Teutonic civilians, women and children, incinerated in the \“Great Trial,\” their screams seemingly still echoing in his ears; and there is the child who drew a family portrait in the ruins, silently questioning him with his innocent eyes. They say nothing, only stare fixedly at him with empty, accusing looks, leaving him nowhere to hide.

He tries to numb himself with strong vodka, but the intoxication only brings a deeper, more tangible terror. In the alcohol-fueled hallucinations, he sees the departed souls crawling out from underground, passing through the walls, gathering by his bed. Their bodies are mutilated; some are still burning, emitting black smoke, others are pierced with tank shrapnel. They reach out with scorched hands, seemingly wanting to grab him and drag him into the bottomless hell where they reside. He can smell the stench of char and rot emanating from them, and feel the bone-chilling cold they bring.

\“Get away! All of you, get away!\” He sits up with a start in the dead of night, pulling out the pistol from under his pillow and firing wildly at the shadows in the room. The gunshots are deafeningly harsh in the silent command post; every bullet sounds like his own death knell. He empties the clip, but the phantoms are completely unharmed, merely looking at him with increasingly sorrowful and mocking eyes. The guards burst in, only to see the Marshal sitting alone in the darkness, disheveled, panting heavily, his eyes bloodshot and filled with the most primal fear of a mortal facing ghosts and gods. They do not know what the Marshal saw, but they can sense that something more dreadful than radiation is utterly consuming the Supreme Commander of the Black League from within.
strings.OMS_yazov_GG.27.desc:
It has been a long time since Yazov truly looked at himself. He had ordered all mirrors removed from his room, as if that would allow him to avoid the monster that haunted him. But today, he has neither drunk alcohol nor taken tranquilizers. He stands soberly on the top floor of the command tower, gazing through the enormous bulletproof glass, overlooking the \“empire\” he created with his own hands.

Omsk, this former Black Citadel, this city that once pulsed with the heart of vengeance, cannot escape the fate of decay. Trash litters the streets, and abandoned vehicles are covered in rust. The buildings are scarred with the wounds of war, like unhealed injuries. The surviving citizens wander like living dead, their faces expressionless, their eyes devoid of light. There is no joy of victory here, no hope of rebuilding, only silence and numbness. Is this what he fought for? A capital of the wasteland built upon hatred and bones? A gigantic, cold tomb?

Clearly reflected on the glass is his weary and distorted image. He looks at the shadow, and the shadow looks back at him. In this moment, he finally stops avoiding, stops struggling. He sees clearly: the monster in his nightmare, the culprit who destroyed everything, is himself. He is not fighting a ghost; he is the greatest ghost, an old-era ghost full of hatred and madness, a specter cursed by his own ideals, wandering over the graveyard he personally created. His reflection perfectly overlaps with the dead silence of the ruins outside the window. He is the ruin, and the ruin is him.

\“They are still hunting me,\” he says to the reflection in the glass, in a voice that is almost calm, barely audible.

\“And I am willing to be eternally tormented by this nightmare.\”

For he knows that this endless pain and torment is the trial he deserves. This is not the end, not even the beginning of the end. This is just the first day of eternal punishment.
strings.OMS_yazov_GG.27.a: If we meet again one day, how shall I greet you? With silence, with tears.
strings.OMS_yazov_GG.26.desc:
The black rain taps against the command post windows, creating a monotonous, hypnotic sound. Yazov has not turned on the lights; he sits quietly in the darkness, listening to the rain outside, letting himself be consumed by this boundless sorrow. In a trance, he seems to see a different scene, a world that never existed, yet is vividly real.

He sees that the war never happened, or perhaps, it ended in a different way. \“He\” leads a unified Russia, dedicated to post-war reconstruction and reconciliation. The factory chimneys emit not black smoke, but the hope of development; in the fields, tractors move through golden waves of wheat, harvesting a bountiful yield; in the cities, children skip and jump with their schoolbags toward bright, clean schools, their laughter as crisp as silver bells. There are no ubiquitous radiation detection stations, no monsters lurking in the shadows, no soldiers in heavy protective suits with numb eyes. People's faces are filled with longing for the future, not fear of tomorrow. They discuss the latest movie releases, complain about the price of bread, instead of where to find a canister of clean water.

\“He\” even sees himself. He is no longer the terrifying \“Leader of the Great Trial,\” perhaps just an old man sent home, a mere footnote in history. In his spare time, he returns to his hometown to teach his grandsons how to fish, telling them which bait works best. He tells them stories of his youth—tales of courage, sacrifice, and camaraderie, not stories of slaughter, destruction, and hatred. He becomes a grandfather respected and loved by children, not a demon king who makes the whole world tremble. What a beautiful world that would be. A world he once had the chance to create but ultimately chose to strangle with his own hands. That warmth, that serenity, is a luxury he could not buy with the entire future of Russia.

'“His” name seems to be “Shu...” something...' Yazov mutters to himself...
strings.OMS_yazov_GG.25.desc:
The beautiful illusion, like a bubble that bursts upon a touch, instantly shatters with the cold brush of reality. Yazov snaps back to his senses, a violent pang of agony seizing his heart. The world outside the window is still the hell shrouded in black rain; the monotonous sound of the rain now sounds like a funeral dirge. Everything he fantasized about was merely a dream, the hopeless craving for salvation from a sinner. The reality is: factories have long shut down, their rusty machinery like the skeletons of prehistoric beasts; the fields are overgrown with mutated weeds, bearing deformed fruits no one dares to eat; the city is an arena where survivors fight for existence, a tragedy of the strong preying on the weak unfolding daily. He has no grandsons; his hands are stained with too much blood, incapable of embracing any warm body.

He stands up, stumbles to the window, and presses his forehead against the cold glass, watching the rainwater carve streaks of black tears onto the pane. He suddenly remembers a line he heard somewhere, a line from a movie: \“All those moments will be lost in time, like tears in rain.\”

Yes, all are lost. The possibility of that brave new world, along with tens of millions of lives, along with the future of the Russian nation, vanished completely the moment he pressed the nuclear button. He once believed he was the creator of history, the savior of Russia, the Michael wielding the sword of vengeance. But now he understands that he is merely a destroyer, a gravedigger who personally buried Russia's future. He dug a gigantic grave and buried his enemies, his compatriots, his ideals, and himself, all within it. The rain blurs his vision, sliding down the wrinkles on his face. He does not know if what is flowing is the black rain outside the window or his own tears. Perhaps, there is no difference anymore.
strings.OMS_yazov_GG.24.desc:
Late at night, Yazov wakes again from a nightmare, his heart pounding frantically in his chest as if trying to break free. He dreams he is back on the day before the war began, back to the moment that changed everything. Karbyshev stands before him, his gaze gentle and firm, just as in his memory. \“Dmitry,\” the mentor's voice is clear and warm, \“Remember, everything we do is to save Russia, to let children laugh freely in a world without fascism, to rebuild a strong and just nation.\”

Then, the scene changes. The warm room vanishes, replaced by an endless expanse of scorched earth. What he sees are collapsed houses, twisted rebar, and children struggling to breathe in the radioactive dust. There is no laughter on their faces, only scorched skin, vacant eyes, and fear of the future. Karbyshev's phantom appears again; this time, he stands upon the ruins, his voice no longer warm, but filled with cold sorrow: \“Dmitry, did you save Russia? Look at these children—are they laughing?\”

Yazov springs up from his cot, cold sweat drenching his uniform. He looks around; the command post is silent, only the map on the wall appears grimly terrifying in the dim light, the red arrows representing destruction like congealed blood. He had always told himself, and everyone else, that everything they did was to carry out Karbyshev's dying wish, to complete the mentor's unfinished work. But now, in the dead of this silent night, he is forced to admit a terrible truth to himself: he was merely using his mentor's name to legitimize his own hatred and ambition. He twisted the mentor's pure ideal of guardianship into an extreme dogma of vengeance. The \“Great Trial\” was never about salvation; it was about destruction from the very beginning. He used a grand lie that everyone was willing to believe to drag all of Russia into an abyss of damnation. He defiled his mentor's sacred name, turning him into an excuse for his own butchery.
strings.OMS_yazov_GG.23.desc:
Yazov staggers to the washroom in the command post, turns the tap, and cold, rusty water flows out. He scoops up a handful of water and splashes it onto his face, trying to use the biting cold to clear himself from the suffocating feeling of the lie. When he looks up and sees the cracked mirror on the wall, he freezes. The person in the mirror is him, yet not him. The face is haggard, aged, the skin lined with deep furrows like a dried-up riverbed. But the most terrifying thing is the eyes: what burns within them is not the flame of an ideal, but a dark, insane, paranoid, empty void that seeks to destroy everything. That is not a savior, but an out-and-out monster.

He remembers his younger self, the young officer wearing the same uniform, listening to Karbyshev's lessons in the military academy. He remembers writing an oath in his diary to liberate all Russian people from suffering and to build a nation that would make his mentor proud. When did he become like this? Was it the moment he made hatred his guiding principle and vengeance his sole program of action? Or was it the fleeting, cold satisfaction he felt upon ordering nuclear bombs dropped on German cities and hearing the news of countless lives instantly vaporized? He can no longer distinguish. He has walked this path for too long, so long that he has forgotten the initial starting point.

He slowly reaches out, his trembling fingertip touching the unfamiliar face in the mirror. The coldness of the mirror sends a shiver down his spine. He suddenly realizes that his greatest enemy was never the Teutons, nor even the internal corrupt elements. His greatest enemy has always been hidden deep within his own heart. In his efforts to fight the abyss, he himself became the abyss, even darker and purer than the one he fought. He won the external war, but he utterly lost the battle against his inner demons. The monster in the mirror is grinning savagely at him, and he has nowhere to run, because that monster is himself.
strings.OMS_yazov_GG.22.desc:
In the underground bunker of the command post, the air is stagnant, heavy as a block of lead. The red markers on the map, representing \“Purified Zones,\” are like countless congealed, bloody eyes, silently mocking the man sitting at the table. Marshal Yazov has not slept for three days; his eye sockets are sunken, and his stubble creeps over his jaw like a patch of gray moss. Before him lies a yellowed old photograph; in it, an elderly man with glasses and a lean face smiles gently, and the young man beside him is Dmitry Yazov.

\“Do you see it? Comrade Karbyshev! Do you see it!\”

A long-suppressed howl bursts without warning from the depths of Yazov's throat—a sound not human, but the tragic cry of a dying beast. He violently sweeps all the files, shell-casing pen holders, and medals off the desk; metal and paper collide and scatter on the concrete floor, creating a jarring cacophony. His trembling finger jabs heavily at the smiling old man's face in the photo, his nail digging deep into the photo paper from the force.

\“Is this the Eden you promised? Is this the pure, grand new world that brooks no impurities, as in your theory?\” he roars, spittle splashing onto the cold map, blurring the blood-red markings. \“I followed your every word, I executed your every concept! I sent the cowards to the gallows, I threw the traitors into the furnace, I reduced the entire old world to ashes! I thought the flame would burn away all filth and forge a brand new Russia! But look out the window! Make me look!\”

He stumbles to the bunker's observation window; beyond that thick door is a world engulfed in eternal nuclear winter. Gray-black snow falls endlessly, covering the ruins of cities and dead forests. There is no birdsong, no sign of life, only the ghost-like moaning of the wind sweeping through the shattered walls and broken ruins.
